events.description: Trump announces Afghanistan strategy promising a 'plan for victory' and warning against hasty withdrawal.
About a year after the Aug 2017 speech, Trump administration began negotiating with the Taliban.
Trump wanted to invite the Taliban to Camp David.
Obama's West Point speech committing to win in Afghanistan, later followed by negotiation with the Taliban.
Obama pulled all US troops out of Iraq; US later redeployed because of the Islamic State.
Trump's West Point graduation speech on ending 'endless wars'; no mention of al-Qaeda.
US R9X Hellfire strike on a vehicle in Idlib, Syria killed Khalid al-Aruri (Abu al-Qasim) and another senior al-Qaeda official.
Abdelmalek Droukdel killed in Mali by French forces with US ISR support; AQIM later confirmed in a ~12 minute video.
Strikes killed three Islamic State commanders in mid-May.
Qasim al-Raymi killed in Yemen; White House issued statement.
AQAP-linked attack in Pensacola, the month before al-Raymi's death.
Joint US-Afghan raid on a Taliban stronghold in Musa Qala killed AQIS emir Asim Umar.
US-Taliban withdrawal deal signed in Doha; Taliban did not renounce al-Qaeda.
Taliban Pashto statement claiming al-Qaeda does not exist in Afghanistan (said not present since days of the Islamic Emirate, 2001), issued after McKenzie's remarks.
CENTCOM's McKenzie said Zawahiri is in eastern Afghanistan and the Taliban must show proof they will fight al-Qaeda.
Internal al-Qaeda 'fitness report' on 19 up-and-coming leaders found in bin Laden files, showing al-Qaeda cadres operating in Afghanistan/Pakistan.
Taliban's Islamic Emirate issued glowing eulogy for Mustafa Abu al-Yazid.
Bin Laden ordered al-Qaeda members out of North Waziristan back into Afghan provinces such as Kunar and Nuristan, to avoid the drone campaign.
Faruq al-Qahtani was killed in a US drone strike in eastern Afghanistan days before the 2016 US presidential election. Al-Qaeda then issued a martyrdom statement.
Trump's speech on Afghanistan strategy in which he promised troops a plan for victory.
Asim Umar was killed in Afghanistan alongside Taliban commanders in late 2019. The DoD declined to publicize it.
McKenzie said Zawahiri is in eastern Afghanistan and that the Taliban must show evidence they will fight al-Qaeda. The Taliban then publicly denied al-Qaeda's presence and blasted McKenzie.
A Resolute Support press release on Asim Umar's death was buried and the DoD chose not to release it (per Roggio, roughly a couple of months before the episode).

key_claims: Gen. McKenzie said Zawahiri is in eastern Afghanistan, and the hosts see this as a major development that drew little attention.
The hosts argue the Taliban should prove their break with al-Qaeda by handing over Zawahiri, and they treat Sirajuddin Haqqani, the Taliban's number two, as deeply tied to al-Qaeda.

Bin Laden's files show he moved al-Qaeda fighters from North Waziristan to Afghan provinces including Kunar and Nuristan around mid-2010, which matches al-Qaeda's later presence in eastern Afghanistan.
Faruq al-Qahtani, an al-Qaeda brigade/battalion head, was killed in eastern Afghanistan in 2016, which they cite as primary-source proof of al-Qaeda's presence there.
The Taliban publicly denied al-Qaeda's presence and blasted McKenzie, and the hosts say the US government made no counter-messaging effort to rebut them.
Asim Umar was killed in late 2019 alongside Taliban commanders, and the DoD buried a Resolute Support press release, which the hosts say would have exposed Taliban-al-Qaeda ties.
The hosts describe a failure of US political and military leadership that whitewashes the Taliban and has lost any plan for victory.
